questions.question: Which scope does a Spring bean have when you add no @Scope annotation?
questions.explanation: Singleton is the default: one shared instance per container.

questions.question: Which scope creates a new bean instance every time the bean is requested from the container?
questions.explanation: A prototype bean is built again on each request, and the container does not track it afterwards.

questions.question: OrderToken is a prototype with a counter that starts at 1. Two calls to context.getBean(OrderToken.class) are stored in a and b, and nothing else created a token. What does a == b print?
questions.explanation: Each getBean call on a prototype builds a new object, so the two references are different.

questions.question: A singleton FreshDesk has a field OrderToken token injected through its constructor, and OrderToken is a prototype. Every customer gets the same token number. Why?
options: The token class is not public
Injection happens once, so the singleton keeps one prototype object
questions.explanation: The prototype is injected only when the singleton is created, so use ObjectProvider to get a new one per call.

questions.question: A singleton service stores the current customer's name in a private field that each request updates. What goes wrong under load?
options: Spring throws an error at startup
Requests overwrite each other's data because they share one object
The service turns into a prototype
questions.explanation: All requests share the single instance, so per-user data in a field leaks between users.
